sanskrit: sa tad rājyam avasthāpya kulūtasahito yayau senābindum atho rājan rājyād āśu samākṣipat
english: Having established that kingdom, he set out together with the Kulūtas, O king, and swiftly wrested Senābindu from his realm.

sanskrit: modāpuraṃ vāmadevaṃ sudāmānaṃ susaṃkulam kulūtān uttarāṃś caiva tāṃś ca rājñaḥ samānayat
english: He brought together Modāpura, Vāmadeva, Sudāman, the populous Susaṃkula, the Kulūtas, the northerners, and all those kings.

sanskrit: tatrasthaḥ puruṣair eva dharmarājasya śāsanāt vyajayad dhanaṃjayo rājan deśān pañca pramāṇataḥ
english: Stationed there and acting by the command of the Dharma-king, Dhanaṃjaya, O king, conquered five regions in due measure.

sanskrit: sa divaḥprastham āsādya senābindoḥ puraṃ mahat balena caturaṅgeṇa niveśam akarot prabhuḥ
english: Having reached Divaḥprastha, the great city of Senābindu, that lord encamped there with his fourfold army.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvair viṣvagaśvaṃ narādhipam abhyagacchan mahātejāḥ pauravaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Surrounded by all of them, that great-splendoured bull among men advanced against the king Viṣvagaśva, the Paurava.

sanskrit: vijitya cāhave śūrān pārvatīyān mahārathān dhvajinyā vyajayad rājan puraṃ pauravarakṣitam
english: Having conquered in battle the heroic mountain-dwellers and great warriors, he conquered with his bannered army, O king, the city guarded by the Paurava.

sanskrit: pauravaṃ tu vinirjitya dasyūn parvatavāsinaḥ gaṇān utsavasaṃketān ajayat sapta pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Having thoroughly conquered the Paurava, the forest-dwelling brigands, and the seven assemblies of the Utsavasaṃketa, that Pāṇḍava prevailed.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāśmīrakān vīrān kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ vyajayal lohitaṃ caiva maṇḍalair daśabhiḥ saha
english: Then that bull among warriors conquered the heroic Kāśmīra warriors along with Lohita and the ten Maṇḍalas.

sanskrit: tatas trigartān kaunteyo dārvān kokanadāś ca ye kṣatriyā bahavo rājann upāvartanta sarvaśaḥ
english: Then the son of Kuntī, O king, caused the Trigartans, the Dārvas, the Kokanadas, and all the many warriors there to submit on every side.

sanskrit: abhisārīṃ tato ramyāṃ vijigye kurunandanaḥ uraśāvāsinaṃ caiva rocamānaṃ raṇe 'jayat
english: Then the joy of the Kurus conquered the lovely Abhisārī and subjugated Rocamāna, the dweller in the Uraśā region, in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ siṃhapuraṃ ramyaṃ citrāyudhasurakṣitam prāmathad balam āsthāya pākaśāsanir āhave
english: Then the son of Pākaśāsana, relying on his forces, crushed the lovely Siṃhapura, well-guarded by Citrāyudha, in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ suhmāṃś ca colāṃś ca kirīṭī pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ sahitaḥ sarvasainyena prāmathat kurunandanaḥ
english: Then Kirīṭī, that bull among Pāṇḍavas, the joy of the Kurus, crushed the Suhmas and the Colas together with his entire army.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramavikrānto bāhlīkān kurunandanaḥ mahatā parimardena vaśe cakre durāsadān
english: Then that supremely valiant joy of the Kurus brought the Bāhlīkas, hard to assail, under his sway by means of great overwhelming force.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā tu balaṃ sāraṃ phalgu cotsṛjya pāṇḍavaḥ daradān saha kāmbojair ajayat pākaśāsaniḥ
english: Retaining the best of the troops and discarding the weaklings, the Pāṇḍava, son of Pākaśāsana, conquered the Daradas together with the Kāmbojas.

sanskrit: prāguttarāṃ diśaṃ ye ca vasanty āśritya dasyavaḥ nivasanti vane ye ca tān sarvān ajayat prabhuḥ
english: Those who dwell in the north-eastern quarter, those brigands, and those who live in the forest — that lord conquered them all.

sanskrit: lohān paramakāmbojān ṛṣikān uttarān api sahitāṃs tān mahārāja vyajayat pākaśāsaniḥ
english: The Lohas, the paramount Kāmbojas, the Ṛṣikas, and the northerners together, O great king — the son of Pākaśāsana conquered them all.

sanskrit: ṛṣikeṣu tu saṃgrāmo babhūvātibhayaṃkaraḥ tārakāmayasaṃkāśaḥ paramarṣikapārthayoḥ
english: Among the Ṛṣikas, however, a most terrifying battle arose between the paramount Ṛṣika lord and Pārtha, resembling the Tārakāmaya war.

sanskrit: sa vijitya tato rājann ṛṣikān raṇamūrdhani śukodarasamaprakhyān hayān aṣṭau samānayat mayūrasadṛśān anyān ubhayān eva cāparān
english: Having conquered the Ṛṣikas in the forefront of battle, O king, he brought back eight horses resembling the belly of a parrot in colour, others resembling peacocks, and yet more of both kinds.

sanskrit: sa vinirjitya saṃgrāme himavantaṃ saniṣkuṭam śvetaparvatam āsādya nyavasat puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Having thoroughly conquered the Himavat range with its forest groves in battle, that bull among men reached the Śveta mountain and encamped there.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa śvetaparvataṃ vīraḥ samatikramya bhārata deśaṃ kiṃpuruṣāvāsaṃ drumaputreṇa rakṣitam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That hero, having crossed the Śveta mountain, O Bhārata, reached the land inhabited by the Kiṃpuruṣas, guarded by the son of Druma.

sanskrit: mahatā saṃnipātena kṣatriyāntakareṇa ha vyajayat pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaḥ kare caiva nyaveśayat
english: With a great clash of armies, that destroyer of warriors, the foremost of Pāṇḍavas, conquered and brought them to submission under tribute.

sanskrit: taṃ jitvā hāṭakaṃ nāma deśaṃ guhyakarakṣitam pākaśāsanir avyagraḥ sahasainyaḥ samāsadat
english: Having conquered him, the son of Pākaśāsana, undistracted, advanced with his army upon the land called Hāṭaka, guarded by the Guhyakas.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sāntvena nirjitya mānasaṃ sara uttamam ṛṣikulyāś ca tāḥ sarvā dadarśa kurunandanaḥ
english: Having subdued them by conciliation, the joy of the Kurus beheld the excellent Lake Mānasa and all those rivers flowing from the sages' settlements.

sanskrit: saro mānasam āsādya hāṭakān abhitaḥ prabhuḥ gandharvarakṣitaṃ deśaṃ vyajayat pāṇḍavas tataḥ
english: Having reached Lake Mānasa, that lord, the Pāṇḍava, then conquered the land around the Hāṭaka region, guarded by the Gandharvas.

sanskrit: tatra tittirikalmāṣān maṇḍūkākṣān hayottamān lebhe sa karam atyantaṃ gandharvanagarāt tadā
english: There he obtained as tribute Tittiri-spotted horses, Maṇḍūkākṣa horses, and the finest steeds from that Gandharva city.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ harivarṣaṃ tu samāsādya sa pāṇḍavaḥ iyeṣa jetuṃ taṃ deśaṃ pākaśāsananandanaḥ
english: Having reached the northern Harivarṣa, that Pāṇḍava, the delight of Pākaśāsana, wished to conquer that land.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ mahākāyā mahāvīryā mahābalāḥ dvārapālāḥ samāsādya hṛṣṭā vacanam abruvan
english: Then the gatekeepers, of mighty frame, great valour, and immense strength, approached him joyfully and spoke these words.

sanskrit: pārtha nedaṃ tvayā śakyaṃ puraṃ jetuṃ kathaṃ cana upāvartasva kalyāṇa paryāptam idam acyuta
english: "O Pārtha, this city cannot be conquered by you in any manner whatsoever. Turn back, O auspicious one — this much is enough, O Acyuta."

sanskrit: idaṃ puraṃ yaḥ praviśed dhruvaṃ sa na bhaven naraḥ prīyāmahe tvayā vīra paryāpto vijayas tava
english: "Whoever enters this city will surely cease to be a mortal being. We are pleased with you, O hero; your conquest is sufficient."

sanskrit: na cāpi kiṃ cij jetavyam arjunātra pradṛśyate uttarāḥ kuravo hy ete nātra yuddhaṃ pravartate
english: "Nor is there anything here for Arjuna to conquer that can be discerned — for these are the northern Kurus, and no battle takes place here."

sanskrit: praviṣṭaś cāpi kaunteya neha drakṣyasi kiṃ cana na hi mānuṣadehena śakyam atrābhivīkṣitum
english: "Even if you were to enter, O son of Kuntī, you would see nothing here, for this place cannot be perceived by one in a human body."

sanskrit: atheha puruṣavyāghra kiṃ cid anyac cikīrṣasi tad bravīhi kariṣyāmo vacanāt tava bhārata
english: "But if you wish to accomplish something else here, O tiger among men, speak it and we shall fulfil it at your word, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tatas tān abravīd rājann arjunaḥ pākaśāsaniḥ pārthivatvaṃ cikīrṣāmi dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then Arjuna, son of Pākaśāsana, spoke to them, O king: "I wish to establish the sovereignty of the wise Dharma-king."

sanskrit: na pravekṣyāmi vo deśaṃ bādhyatvaṃ yadi mānuṣaiḥ yudhiṣṭhirāya yat kiṃ cit karavan naḥ pradīyatām
english: "I shall not enter your land, nor impose the burden of subjugation by mortals — let whatever tribute pleasing to Yudhiṣṭhira be given to us."

sanskrit: tato divyāni vastrāṇi divyāny ābharaṇāni ca mokājināni divyāni tasmai te pradaduḥ karam
english: Then they presented him as tribute divine garments, divine ornaments, and divine skins of the Moka deer.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa puruṣavyāghro vijigye diśam uttarām saṃgrāmān subahūn kṛtvā kṣatriyair dasyubhis tathā
english: Thus that tiger among men conquered the northern quarter, having fought very many battles against warriors and against brigands alike.

sanskrit: sa vinirjitya rājñas tān kare ca viniveśya ha dhanāny ādāya sarvebhyo ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: Having thoroughly conquered those kings and placed them under tribute, he took from all of them wealth and various kinds of gems.

sanskrit: hayāṃs tittirikalmāṣāñ śukapatranibhān api mayūrasadṛśāṃś cānyān sarvān anilaraṃhasaḥ
english: Horses spotted like the Tittiri bird, others resembling the wing of a parrot, others resembling peacocks — all of them swift as the wind.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ sumahatā rājan balena caturaṅgiṇā ājagāma punar vīraḥ śakraprasthaṃ purottamam
english: Surrounded by a very great fourfold army, O king, that hero returned once more to the foremost of cities, Śakraprastha.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu bhīmaseno 'pi vīryavān dharmarājam anujñāpya yayau prācīṃ diśaṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At this very same time the valiant Bhīmasena also, having taken leave of the Dharma-king, set out towards the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: mahatā balacakreṇa pararāṣṭrāvamardinā vṛto bharataśārdūlo dviṣacchokavivardhanaḥ
english: Accompanied by a great wheel of forces that crushed enemy kingdoms, that tiger of the Bharatas, increaser of foes' grief, marched forth.

sanskrit: sa gatvā rājaśārdūlaḥ pāñcālānāṃ puraṃ mahat pāñcālān vividhopāyaiḥ sāntvayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: That tiger among kings, the Pāṇḍava, going to the great city of the Pāñcālas, pacified the Pāñcālas by various means.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa gaṇḍakīṃ śūro videhāṃś ca nararṣabhaḥ vijityālpena kālena daśārṇān agamat prabhuḥ
english: Then that hero, bull among men, having conquered the Gaṇḍakī and the Videhas in a short time, that lord advanced to the Daśārṇas.

sanskrit: tatra dāśārṇako rājā sudharmā lomaharṣaṇam kṛtavān karma bhīmena mahad yuddhaṃ nirāyudham
english: There the Dāśārṇaka king Sudharmā performed a hair-raising feat — he fought a great unarmed battle with Bhīma.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu tad dṛṣṭvā tasya karma paraṃtapaḥ adhisenāpatiṃ cakre sudharmāṇaṃ mahābalam
english: But Bhīmasena, the scorcher of foes, seeing that feat of his, made the mighty Sudharmā his commander of the army.

sanskrit: tataḥ prācīṃ diśaṃ bhīmo yayau bhīmaparākramaḥ sainyena mahatā rājan kampayann iva medinīm
english: Then Bhīma of fearful valour marched towards the eastern quarter with a great army, O king, as if shaking the earth.

sanskrit: so 'śvamedheśvaraṃ rājan rocamānaṃ sahānujam jigāya samare vīro balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: He, the best of the strong, O king, conquered in battle the lord of the Aśvamedha sacrifice, Rocamāna, together with his younger brother.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nirjitya kaunteyo nātitīvreṇa karmaṇā pūrvadeśaṃ mahāvīryo vijigye kurunandanaḥ
english: Having conquered him without overly fierce action, that son of Kuntī of great heroism, the joy of the Kurus, subdued the eastern land.

sanskrit: tato dakṣiṇam āgamya pulindanagaraṃ mahat sukumāraṃ vaśe cakre sumitraṃ ca narādhipam
english: Then coming southward, he brought under his sway the great city of the Pulindas and the delicate Sumitra, lord of men.

sanskrit: tatas tu dharmarājasya śāsanād bharatarṣabhaḥ śiśupālaṃ mahāvīryam abhyayāj janamejaya
english: Then by the command of the Dharma-king, O Janamejaya, that bull of the Bharatas advanced against the mighty Śiśupāla.

sanskrit: cedirājo 'pi tac chrutvā pāṇḍavasya cikīrṣitam upaniṣkramya nagarāt pratyagṛhṇāt paraṃtapaḥ
english: The Cedi king too, hearing what the Pāṇḍava intended, came out from the city and received him, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tau sametya mahārāja kurucedivṛṣau tadā ubhayor ātmakulayoḥ kauśalyaṃ paryapṛcchatām
english: Those two meeting, O great king — the bulls of the Kuru and the Cedi — enquired about the well-being of each other's families.

sanskrit: tato nivedya tad rāṣṭraṃ cedirājo viśāṃ pate uvāca bhīmaṃ prahasan kim idaṃ kuruṣe 'nagha
english: Then, having offered his kingdom, the Cedi king, O lord of the people, said to Bhīma with a laugh: "What is this you are doing, O sinless one?"

sanskrit: tasya bhīmas tadācakhyau dharmarājacikīrṣitam sa ca tat pratigṛhyaiva tathā cakre narādhipaḥ
english: Bhīma then told him of the Dharma-king's intention, and that lord of men, accepting it, acted accordingly.

sanskrit: tato bhīmas tatra rājann uṣitvā tridaśāḥ kṣapāḥ satkṛtaḥ śiśupālena yayau sabalavāhanaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, O king, having stayed there thirty nights and been honoured by Śiśupāla, departed with his forces and conveyances.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kumāraviṣaye śreṇimantam athājayat kosalādhipatiṃ caiva bṛhadbalam ariṃdamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then in the Kumāra region that subduer of foes conquered Śreṇimān and also Bṛhadbala, lord of Kosala.

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāṃ tu dharmajñaṃ dīrghaprajñaṃ mahābalam ajayat pāṇḍavaśreṣṭho nātitīvreṇa karmaṇā
english: At Ayodhyā, the foremost of Pāṇḍavas conquered the righteous, far-sighted, and mighty king without overly fierce action.

sanskrit: tato gopālakacchaṃ ca sottamān api cottarān mallānām adhipaṃ caiva pārthivaṃ vyajayat prabhuḥ
english: Then that lord conquered Gopālakaccha, the excellent and northern Mallakas, and also the king who was lord of the Mallas.

sanskrit: tato himavataḥ pārśve samabhyetya jaradgavam sarvam alpena kālena deśaṃ cakre vaśe balī
english: Then approaching the slopes of the Himavat and reaching Jaradgava, that strong one brought the entire region under his sway in a short time.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhān deśān vijitya puruṣarṣabhaḥ unnāṭam abhito jigye kukṣimantaṃ ca parvatam pāṇḍavaḥ sumahāvīryo balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: Having thus conquered many and various lands, that bull among men, the Pāṇḍava of very great heroism, best of the strong, also conquered all around Unnāṭa and the mountain Kukṣimanta.

sanskrit: sa kāśirājaṃ samare subandhum anivartinam vaśe cakre mahābāhur bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: The long-armed Bhīma of fearful valour brought under his sway in battle the king of Kāśī, Subandhu, who never retreated.

sanskrit: tataḥ supārśvam abhitas tathā rājapatiṃ kratham yudhyamānaṃ balāt saṃkhye vijigye pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: Then that bull among Pāṇḍavas conquered all around Supārśva and also Kratha, lord of kings, who fought with all his might in the engagement.

sanskrit: tato matsyān mahātejā malayāṃś ca mahābalān anavadyān gayāṃś caiva paśubhūmiṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then the greatly splendoured one conquered the Matsyas, the mighty and blameless Malayas, the Gayas, and the Paśubhūmi in its entirety.

sanskrit: nivṛtya ca mahābāhur madarvīkaṃ mahīdharam sopadeśaṃ vinirjitya prayayāv uttarāmukhaḥ vatsabhūmiṃ ca kaunteyo vijigye balavān balāt
english: The long-armed one, turning back, thoroughly conquered Madarvīka mountain with its surrounding region and marched northward; and the son of Kuntī, mighty in strength, conquered the Vatsabhūmi by force.

sanskrit: bhargāṇām adhipaṃ caiva niṣādādhipatiṃ tathā vijigye bhūmipālāṃś ca maṇimatpramukhān bahūn
english: He also conquered the lord of the Bhārgas, the lord of the Niṣādas, and many rulers of the earth with Maṇimān at their head.

sanskrit: tato dakṣiṇamallāṃś ca bhogavantaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ tarasaivājayad bhīmo nātitīvreṇa karmaṇā
english: Then the Pāṇḍava Bhīma swiftly conquered the southern Mallas and the Bhogavanta without overly fierce action.

sanskrit: śarmakān varmakāṃś caiva sāntvenaivājayat prabhuḥ vaidehakaṃ ca rājānaṃ janakaṃ jagatīpatim vijigye puruṣavyāghro nātitīvreṇa karmaṇā
english: That lord conquered the Śarmakas and the Varmakas by conciliation alone; and that tiger among men conquered without overly fierce action Janaka, the Vaideha king, lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vaidehasthas tu kaunteya indraparvatam antikāt kirātānām adhipatīn vyajayat sapta pāṇḍavaḥ
english: While stationed in the Videha land, the Pāṇḍava son of Kuntī conquered from nearby Indraparvata seven lords of the Kirātas.

sanskrit: tataḥ suhmān prācyasuhmān samakṣāṃś caiva vīryavān vijitya yudhi kaunteyo māgadhān upayād balī
english: Then the valiant son of Kuntī, having conquered the Suhmas, the Eastern Suhmas, and the Samakṣas in battle, that strong one advanced upon the Māgadhas.

sanskrit: daṇḍaṃ ca daṇḍadhāraṃ ca vijitya pṛthivīpatīn tair eva sahitaḥ sarvair girivrajam upādravat
english: Having conquered Daṇḍa and Daṇḍadhāra and the lords of the earth, together with all of them he advanced upon Girivraja.

sanskrit: jārāsaṃdhiṃ sāntvayitvā kare ca viniveśya ha tair eva sahito rājan karṇam abhyadravad balī
english: Having conciliated Jārāsaṃdhi and placed him under tribute, that strong one, O king, advanced against Karṇa together with all of them.

sanskrit: sa kampayann iva mahīṃ balena caturaṅgiṇā yuyudhe pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaḥ karṇenāmitraghātinā
english: Shaking the earth as it were with his fourfold army, that foremost of Pāṇḍavas battled with Karṇa, slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ yudhi nirjitya vaśe kṛtvā ca bhārata tato vijigye balavān rājñaḥ parvatavāsinaḥ
english: Having conquered Karṇa in battle and brought him to submission, O Bhārata, that strong one then conquered the mountain-dwelling kings.

sanskrit: atha modāgiriṃ caiva rājānaṃ balavattaram pāṇḍavo bāhuvīryeṇa nijaghāna mahāmṛdhe
english: Then the Pāṇḍava struck down in the great battle the even mightier king of Modāgiri by the strength of his arms.

sanskrit: tataḥ pauṇḍrādhipaṃ vīraṃ vāsudevaṃ mahābalam kauśikīkacchanilayaṃ rājānaṃ ca mahaujasam
english: Then the heroic, mighty Vāsudeva, lord of the Pauṇḍras, and the king of great energy who dwelt on the bank of the Kauśikī river —

sanskrit: ubhau balavṛtau vīrāv ubhau tīvraparākramau nirjityājau mahārāja vaṅgarājam upādravat
english: Both surrounded by forces, both heroes, both of fierce valour — having conquered those two in battle, O great king, he advanced upon the king of Vaṅga.

sanskrit: samudrasenaṃ nirjitya candrasenaṃ ca pārthivam tāmraliptaṃ ca rājānaṃ kācaṃ vaṅgādhipaṃ tathā
english: Having conquered Samudrasena, the king Candrasena, the king of Tāmralipta, and Kāca the lord of Vaṅga —

sanskrit: suhmānām adhipaṃ caiva ye ca sāgaravāsinaḥ sarvān mlecchagaṇāṃś caiva vijigye bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: And the lord of the Suhmas, those who dwell by the ocean, and all the troops of Mlecchas — that bull of the Bharatas conquered them all.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhān deśān vijitya pavanātmajaḥ vasu tebhya upādāya lauhityam agamad balī
english: Having thus conquered many and various lands and taken wealth from them, the mighty son of the Wind-god advanced to the Lauhitya river.

sanskrit: sa sarvān mlecchanṛpatīn sāgaradvīpavāsinaḥ karam āhārayām āsa ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: He made all the Mleccha kings and those dwelling on the ocean islands pay tribute and various kinds of gems.
